content_html_sanitized:
Olympia, Washington

A bill that would legalize the medical use of marijuana was offered by Sen. Jeanne Kohl as a much narrower version of the ballot initiative that was rejected by Washington voters last fall.

Senate Bill 6271 would provide legal immunity to patients who use marijuana, physicians who recommend it and pharmacists who provide it. Of course, there is no way for pharmacists to get it. The bill also would create a campaign to inform youth that marijuana use is illegal, except in cases involving authorized use by seriously ill people under a physician's care. Since the bill is unlikely to pass perhaps the Senate would pass a bill that explains to youth why being arrested is good for sick people.
